correctness.rationale: Translation of perfect edge domination to three local Boolean clauses for rung, top rail and bottom rail edges is exact; selected edges have no constraint. The binary three-column transfer graph on pairs of 3-bit labels has 42 active pair states and 102 arcs, with exactly two cyclic strongly connected components: the 7→7 fixed loop and the six-state cycle (0,1)→(1,5)→(5,0)→(0,2)→(2,6)→(6,0). Any closed walk lies entirely in a cyclic SCC; only six-cycle length divisible by six contributes six labelled phases, one selected bit per column, while all-7 selects 3n. The 8³=512 transition cases are exhaustive finite classification, not a sample of graph sizes; independent rebuild of this transfer graph and SCCs reproduced its cyclic structure, and independent direct edge-subset enumeration n=3..6 gave exactly the claimed counts.

final_claim: For labeled prism graphs C_n□K2 (n>=3), the perfect edge domination generating polynomial, counting F such that every unselected edge has exactly one selected neighboring edge, is z^(3n)+6 1_{6|n} z^n; the six proper solutions are precisely the cyclic phases of the edge-column word (0,1,5,0,2,6).
limitations: Unweighted perfect edge domination of labeled prisms only; not vertex perfect domination, ordinary edge domination, or all generalized Petersen graphs.
